facts.statement: Noripterus is a genus of dsungaripterid pterodactyloid pterosaur whose name means "lake wing".
facts.quote: Noripterus (meaning "lake wing" from Mongolian nuur, "lake" and Greek pteron, "wing") is a genus of dsungaripterid pterodactyloid pterosaur from Lower Cretaceous of Asia.

facts.statement: Noripterus was estimated to be one-third shorter than the contemporaneous Dsungaripterus.
facts.quote: Noripterus was quite similar to the contemporaneous Dsungaripterus, though it was estimated to be a third shorter.

facts.statement: Noripterus possessed long, narrow neck vertebrae, a crest, and a toothless front lower jaw.
facts.quote: It has long narrow neck vertebrae and, like Dsungaripterus, a crest and no teeth in the front of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The teeth present in Noripterus were well-developed and spaced far apart.
facts.quote: The teeth that are present are well-developed and spaced fairly far apart.

facts.statement: Noripterus had a straight, sharp snout that did not point upwards like that of Dsungaripterus.
facts.quote: The sharp snout is straight and not pointed upwards as with Dsungaripterus.

facts.statement: Noripterus was first named by Yang Zhongjian in 1973.
facts.quote: It was first named by Yang Zhongjian (also known as C.C. Young in older sources) in 1973.

facts.statement: The type species, Noripterus complicidens, was found in the Lianmuqin and Shengjinkou Formations of the Junggar Basin in Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: The type species, Noripterus complidicens, is from the Wuerho Pterosaur Fauna (WPF) of the Lianmuqin Formation and Shengjinkou Formation in the Junggar Basin of Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The species Noripterus parvus was recovered from the Tsagaantsav Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: The second species, Noripterus parvus, was recovered from the Tsagaantsav Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Data suggests at least some deposits containing Noripterus date to the middle Valanginian, though the exact age bounds remain unclear.
facts.quote: Both formations have seen various age estimates, with data suggest at least some of the WPF dates to the middle Valanginian, but the upper and lower bounds of these pterosaur bearing deposits remains unclear.

facts.statement: Noripterus lived alongside the larger Dsungaripterus in environments with extensive inland lake systems.
facts.quote: Noripterus lived in the same time and place as the larger Dsungaripterus, in formations that indicate the presence of extensive inland lake systems.

facts.statement: Noripterus is assigned to the family Dsungaripteridae due to its similarity to Dsungaripterus.
facts.quote: Because of its similarity to Dsungaripterus, Noripterus has been assigned to the family Dsungaripteridae.

facts.statement: A 2019 study by Kellner and colleagues recovered Noripterus outside Azhdarchoidea within Tapejaroidea as a sister taxon to Dsungaripterus.
facts.quote: Their cladogram is shown below. In 2019, a different topology, this time by Kellner and colleagues, was published. In this study, Noripterus was recovered outside the Azhdarchoidea, within the larger group Tapejaroidea, sister taxon to Dsungaripterus.

facts.statement: The genus Phobetor was originally described by Natasha Bakhurina in 1982 based on a single leg bone.
facts.quote: El género Phobetor, nombrado por el dios griego de las pesadillas, fue descrito originalmente en 1982 por Natasha Bakhurina como una especie de Dsungaripterus (D. parvus), basándose en un único hueso de la pata, PIN 3953.

facts.statement: The genus name Phobetor was unavailable because it was previously used as a synonym for the fish Gymnocanthus tricuspis.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el nombre del género Phobetor ya había sido usado como un sinónimo más moderno de la especie Gymnocanthus tricuspis (sinónimo más antiguo de "Phobetor tricuspis" Krøyer, 1844), un pez del orden de los escorpeniformes, y por lo tanto no estaba disponible.

facts.statement: In 2009, Lü and colleagues found Phobetor indistinguishable from Noripterus and referred it as a junior synonym.
facts.quote: En 2009, Lü y colegas reexaminaron la mayor parte del material fósil conocido de dsungariptéridos, y hallaron que "Phobetor" era indistinguible de Noripterus, causando que lo refirieran a este como un sinónimo más moderno.

facts.statement: Noripterus lived from the Valanginian to the Barremian, between 137.05 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Barremian (137.05 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is likely that Noripterus and Dsungaripterus occupied separate ecological niches due to differences in skull robustness and tooth strength.
facts.quote: Because Noripterus had a more lightly built skull with weaker, more slender teeth than its larger contemporary, it is likely that the two pterosaurs occupied separate ecological niches.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Dsungaripterus hunted in shallow lakes eating hard-shelled animals, while Noripterus fed on fish in deeper lake regions.
facts.quote: Noripterus vivió en el mismo tiempo y lugar que el mucho mayor Dsungaripterus, en formaciones que indican la presencia de extensos sistemas de lagos de tierra adentro. Debido a que Noripterus tenía un cráneo de constitución más ligera y débil con dientes más delgados que los de su contemporáneo, es probable que los dos pterosaurios ocuparan nichos ecológicos separados, con Dsungaripterus cazando en las partes someras de los lagos y comiendo animales de conchas duras, mientras que Noripterus se alimentaba de peces en las regiones más profundas de los lagos.

rejected.statement: Noripterus is interpreted as adapted for feeding on shellfish or hard foodstuffs using a long, toothless beak tip for probing and robust rear teeth for cracking shells.
rejected.quote: Dsungaripterids like Noripterus are interpreted as adapted for feeding on shellfish or other hard foodstuffs, with long narrow toothless beak tips for probing and picking up suitable prey, and robust teeth farther back for cracking shells.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'interpreted as adapted for feeding on shellfish or'

rejected.statement: Noripterus was well adapted to a terrestrial lifestyle, featuring thick bone walls and stout bodily proportions.
rejected.quote: Like most dsungaripteroids, Noripterus was well adapted to a terrestrial lifestyle, bearing thick bone walls and stouty bodily proportions.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Noripterus was well adapted to a terrestrial lifestyle'

rejected.statement: Hone and colleagues (2017) claim there are notable differences between the limbs of Noripterus and Phobetor, suggesting a detailed description of Phobetor is needed to clarify their relationship.
rejected.quote: However, in a 2017 review of the holotype and additional specimens of Noripterus, Hone and colleagues claim there are "notable differences" between the limbs of Noripterus and 'Phobetor,' and that a detailed description of the latter is necessary to clarify these relationships.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'claim there are notable differences between the limbs'

rejected.statement: Assigning Phobetor material to Noripterus increases the known maximum wingspan to 4 meters.
rejected.quote: Al asignar el material de "Phobetor" a Noripterus se incrementa el tamaño conocido de este último indicando que alcanzaría una envergadura máxima de cuatro metros.
